# opencode-cleanup development

Build an English-language OpenCode TUI plugin. Target the tested OpenCode
1.18.34 API, OpenTUI 0.4.5 and Solid 1.9.12. Use current official types, not
old community examples. Fetch current documentation when changing host APIs.

Read `.opencode/skills/opencode-tui-development/SKILL.md` for UI work and
`.opencode/skills/opencode-storage-maintenance/SKILL.md` for storage changes.

## Invariants

- Analysis is read-only; never migrate or create a user OpenCode database.
- Run expensive SQLite scans in a separate process, never in the TUI thread.
- A DB is identified by canonical path, file identity and schema signature.
  Show that identity to the user. Ambiguous/remote targets require an explicit
  database choice. An API session list is not a global DB session inventory.
- Disk bytes, logical UTF-8 payload bytes and process RAM are different metrics.
  Do not promise that logical deletions immediately shrink a SQLite file.
- Cleanup has a frozen preview and execution-time revalidation. Do not expand
  an approved plan after the preview. Protect current/busy/pinned/latest sessions
  and recursively protected descendants. Protect shared snapshots conservatively.
- All destructive changes run after OpenCode closes, with a verified SQLite
  backup and a verified streaming archive before any deletion.
- Event history is persistent source data. No session row does not imply garbage.
  Preserve identities, event sequences, unknown event types and provider metadata.
- Use parameterized SQL, foreign keys, bounded batches, transactions and real
  filesystem paths. Reject symlinks/junctions and files outside the managed root.
- Never delete WAL/SHM files manually or replace a DB file while clients use it.
- Cancel/timeout/error paths release workers and UI registrations. Interrupted
  jobs must report their actual committed changes; never blindly rerun them.
- Never run cleanup against the developer's real database as a test.

## Verification

Use meaningful tests with real temporary SQLite databases and directories.
Test stale plans, child protection, unknown schemas, archives, rollback,
unreferenced files, delayed jobs, interrupted execution and schema variants.
Run `npm run check`, `npm run test:tui`, and a built worker smoke check before
claiming completion. No subagents are needed for this project.

## Packaging

Export `./tui` with default `{ id, tui }`. Register palette commands with
`api.keymap.registerLayer`. Keep host Solid/OpenTUI packages external in the
build. Project skills are development guidance, not runtime plugin dependencies.

# OpenCode storage maintenance

## Analysis

Discover data roots via XDG_DATA_HOME, OPENCODE_DB and an explicit configured
path. Show all channel DB candidates, but never infer the active DB from size.
Open SQLite read-only. Inspect sqlite_master and table_info before querying.
Report legacy message/part and newer session_message separately from durable
event/event_sequence data. Use length(cast(data as blob)) for UTF-8 bytes.
Use page_count, page_size, freelist_count and optional dbstat for physical bytes.
Use limited scans and explicit deep analysis. RSS is process-wide, not per session.

## Cleanup

Preview exact session IDs, child closure, event aggregates, reasoning objects
and file identities. Filters combine with AND, with last activity as default age.
Pin protection is DB-scoped, persistent and reread by the maintenance worker.
A protected child prevents deleting its ancestor via a recursive host operation.

Run cleanup only after host processes exit and a quiet-period check succeeds.
Take a SQLite online backup, run quick_check on it, archive selected source
records to JSONL gzip and verify their digest/count. Then begin a write
transaction and revalidate the approved fingerprint before mutation.

Delete a session's events and dependent tables together. For reasoning cleanup,
redact only schema-understood text payloads in projections and corresponding
durable events; keep event IDs, sequence numbers, model/provider metadata and
other message content intact. Abort on malformed/unsupported affected records.
Never label detached event histories as disposable automatically.

Check file realpaths and reject symlinks/junctions, changed files and files
referenced by retained messages/events. Snapshot roots are shared by project;
never delete snapshots of a project with retained or protected history.

VACUUM is optional compaction, not deletion. Check disk space for backup,
archives and temporary DB pages. Never unlink a WAL to shrink a database.
Keep a durable job report and recover interrupted states without reapplying.

References:
- https://github.com/whtsky/ocgc
- https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/tree/dev/packages/core/src/session
- https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/core/src/event.ts
- https://www.sqlite.org/backup.html
- https://www.sqlite.org/lang_vacuum.html
- https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html

# OpenCode TUI development

1. Verify `@opencode-ai/plugin/tui` types for the target host. Current baseline:
   OpenCode 1.18.34, OpenTUI 0.4.5, SolidJS 1.9.12.
2. Export a default `{ id: "opencode-cleanup", tui }` from the `./tui` entrypoint.
   A TUI module must not also export `server`.
3. Use `api.keymap.registerLayer` with `namespace: "palette"`. Ctrl+P belongs
   to the host. Use `api.ui.dialog.replace`, `api.ui.DialogSelect` and actual
   Solid/OpenTUI JSX for integrated screens. No browser or LLM prompt is needed.
4. Every sub-screen has a clickable Back action. Use compact terminal layouts,
   scrollable content, host theme colors and loading/error/empty states.
5. Cleanup registrations and subprocesses with component cleanup and the host's
   lifecycle. Do not leave refresh intervals running while dialogs are closed.
6. Compile Solid with `babel-preset-solid`, `generate: "universal"`, moduleName
   `@opentui/solid`; do not bundle a second host Solid runtime.
7. Exercise the built entrypoint and command callbacks, then use the real OpenTUI
   test renderer for frame output, Back navigation and narrow terminal layouts.

Authoritative references:
- https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/specs/tui-plugins.md
- https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/plugin/src/tui.ts
- https://opencode.ai/tui.json
- https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/blob/main/packages/web/src/content/SKILL.md
- https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/blob/main/packages/web/src/content/docs/core-concepts/testing.mdx

The official OpenTUI skill is the layout/testing reference. Older community
server-plugin skills often describe pre-TUI limitations; confirm against host
types before adopting their advice.

# opencode-cleanup

[Русский](README.ru.md)

An English-language TUI plugin for inspecting OpenCode storage and scheduling database maintenance from inside OpenCode.

## Features

- Dashboard for SQLite files, WAL/SHM, sessions, event history, snapshots, session diffs, tool output and OpenCode process memory.
- Session inspection and storage breakdown by part type.
- Database identity reporting: canonical path and schema signature.
- Background maintenance worker with verified SQLite backups and streaming, checksum-verified JSONL gzip archives.
- Installer that preserves other plugins and JSONC comments, plus a standalone uninstaller.

The selective-cleanup screen is a preliminary interface: it does not yet expose a complete filter, approval and execution flow. The maintenance command queues detached-history archiving and database compaction. Read [compatibility and limitations](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) before use.

## Installation

Install Node.js and OpenCode with TUI plugin support. Detailed runtime requirements are listed in [compatibility](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md).

Download the ZIP from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/demyanovvvv/opencode-cleanup/releases) and extract it. On Windows, double-click `install.cmd`. From the extracted directory on other platforms, run:

```bash
node scripts/setup.mjs install
```

Alternatively, clone the repository and run the installer from the checkout:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/demyanovvvv/opencode-cleanup.git
cd opencode-cleanup
npm run install:plugin
```

The source installer prepares dependencies and builds the plugin. The release ZIP already contains the compiled files. The installer registers the plugin in `tui.json` or `tui.jsonc` and prints its installed location. Quit and restart OpenCode after installation.

## Usage

Open the command palette with `Ctrl+P` and select:

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `Cleanup: Dashboard` | Storage overview and process memory |
| `Cleanup: Sessions` | Session list and logical payload sizes |
| `Cleanup: Analyze storage` | Part types and detached event-history counts |
| `Cleanup: Selective cleanup` | Preliminary session-protection interface |
| `Cleanup: Database maintenance` | Queue archival and compaction after OpenCode closes |

`Ctrl+Shift+O` opens the dashboard. Sub-screens have a clickable Back action.

Disk usage, logical UTF-8 payload size and process RAM are separate measurements. Deleting records does not immediately shrink a SQLite file; compaction is a separate operation. A detached event history is still persistent source data.

Before queueing maintenance, check the displayed database identity. After queueing, close OpenCode so the worker can proceed. Keep the generated backups, archives and job report until you have reviewed the result.

## Configuration

The installer respects `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME` and `OPENCODE_TUI_CONFIG`. To select custom locations:

```bash
node scripts/setup.mjs install --config-dir "/path/to/config" --data-dir "/path/to/data"
```

Use `--config <file>` for a specific TUI configuration and `--source <directory>` for the package source. The database path comes from `OPENCODE_DB` when set, otherwise from the host state path. Prefer an explicit absolute database path when using custom storage.

## Uninstall

On Windows, double-click `uninstall.cmd`, or run from the extracted package or checkout:

```bash
node scripts/setup.mjs uninstall
```

The installed plugin directory also contains standalone `uninstall.cmd` and `uninstall.mjs` launchers, so removal remains possible without the original package folder.

The uninstaller removes plugin registrations, installed plugin files, settings and job registrations. It requests cancellation of queued workers and waits for them to exit. If a worker is still finishing its transaction after the timeout, retry removal afterward. **History archives and SQLite backups are preserved.** Quit and restart OpenCode to unload the plugin.

Windows launchers accept `--no-pause` for terminal use.

# opencode-cleanup

[English](README.md)

TUI-плагин с англоязычным интерфейсом для просмотра хранилища OpenCode и постановки обслуживания базы данных в очередь прямо из OpenCode.

## Возможности

- Панель с данными SQLite, WAL/SHM, сессиями, историей событий, снимками, различиями сессий, выводом инструментов и памятью процессов OpenCode.
- Просмотр сессий и распределения объёма данных по типам частей сообщений.
- Отображение идентичности базы: канонического пути и сигнатуры схемы.
- Фоновое обслуживание с проверенными резервными копиями SQLite и потоковыми архивами JSONL gzip с проверкой контрольных сумм.
- Установщик, сохраняющий другие плагины и комментарии JSONC, и автономный деинсталлятор.

Экран выборочной очистки — предварительный интерфейс: полный сценарий выбора фильтров, подтверждения и выполнения пока не доступен. Команда обслуживания ставит в очередь архивирование отсоединённой истории и уплотнение базы. Перед использованием прочитайте [требования и ограничения](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md).

## Установка

Установите Node.js и OpenCode с поддержкой TUI-плагинов. Подробные требования приведены в [документе о совместимости](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md).

Скачайте ZIP из [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/demyanovvvv/opencode-cleanup/releases) и распакуйте. На Windows дважды щёлкните `install.cmd`. На других платформах выполните из распакованной папки:

```bash
node scripts/setup.mjs install
```

Также можно клонировать репозиторий и запустить установщик из исходников:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/demyanovvvv/opencode-cleanup.git
cd opencode-cleanup
npm run install:plugin
```

При установке из исходников установщик подготавливает зависимости и собирает плагин. ZIP уже содержит собранные файлы. Установщик регистрирует плагин в `tui.json` или `tui.jsonc` и выводит путь установки. После установки полностью закройте и заново запустите OpenCode.

## Использование

Откройте палитру команд сочетанием `Ctrl+P` и выберите:

| Команда | Назначение |
| --- | --- |
| `Cleanup: Dashboard` | Обзор хранилища и памяти процессов |
| `Cleanup: Sessions` | Список сессий и логический объём данных |
| `Cleanup: Analyze storage` | Типы частей сообщений и отсоединённая история событий |
| `Cleanup: Selective cleanup` | Предварительный интерфейс защиты сессий |
| `Cleanup: Database maintenance` | Архивирование и уплотнение после закрытия OpenCode |

`Ctrl+Shift+O` открывает панель. На вложенных экранах есть кнопка Back.

Размер на диске, логический объём UTF-8 и оперативная память процесса — разные показатели. Удаление записей не уменьшает файл SQLite немедленно; уплотнение выполняется отдельно. Отсоединённая история событий остаётся исходными сохранёнными данными.

Перед постановкой обслуживания в очередь проверьте показанную идентичность базы. После постановки закройте OpenCode, чтобы фоновый процесс мог продолжить работу. Сохраняйте резервные копии, архивы и отчёт задания до проверки результата.

## Настройка

Установщик учитывает `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME` и `OPENCODE_TUI_CONFIG`. Для собственных каталогов:

```bash
node scripts/setup.mjs install --config-dir "/path/to/config" --data-dir "/path/to/data"
```

`--config <file>` задаёт файл конфигурации TUI, а `--source <directory>` — папку пакета. Путь базы берётся из `OPENCODE_DB`, если переменная задана, иначе — из пути состояния хоста. Для нестандартного хранилища предпочтителен явно заданный абсолютный путь к базе.

## Удаление

На Windows дважды щёлкните `uninstall.cmd` либо выполните из папки пакета или исходников:

```bash
node scripts/setup.mjs uninstall
```

В установленной папке плагина также находятся автономные `uninstall.cmd` и `uninstall.mjs`: исходная папка пакета для удаления не нужна.

Деинсталлятор удаляет регистрации плагина, установленные файлы, настройки и регистрации заданий. Он запрашивает отмену заданий и ожидает завершения фоновых процессов. Если процесс продолжает завершать транзакцию после тайм-аута, повторите удаление позже. **Архивы истории и резервные копии SQLite сохраняются.** Полностью перезапустите OpenCode, чтобы выгрузить плагин.

Для запуска Windows-скриптов из терминала без паузы используйте `--no-pause`.

# Contributing

Thank you for helping improve opencode-cleanup. Check existing issues before reporting a problem or proposing a change. Use [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for vulnerability reports.

## Development setup

Use the runtimes listed in [compatibility](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md), including Bun for the TUI renderer tests.

```bash
npm ci
npm run check
npm run test:tui
npm run smoke:worker
npm run smoke:installer
```

`check` runs type checking, Node tests and the build. TUI tests exercise the built entrypoint, so build before running them in isolation. Smoke checks use temporary SQLite databases and directories.

## Project structure

- `src/tui.tsx` and `src/tui/`: OpenCode plugin entrypoint and screens.
- `src/analysis/`: database inspection and formatting.
- `src/cleanup/`: session protection and cleanup planning.
- `src/maintenance/` and `src/worker/`: archives, backups and queued jobs.
- `src/install/`: installation, configuration editing and removal.
- `scripts/`: build, setup and built-artifact checks.
- `tests/`: automated checks.

Read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) and the project development skills in `.opencode/skills/` before changing storage or TUI code. Fetch official host API documentation when changing integrations.

## Storage and UI invariants

Analysis must be read-only. Never run destructive tests against your own OpenCode database. Use real temporary databases and filesystem fixtures. Preserve durable event identities and unknown source data. Revalidate approved plans at execution time. Verify backups and streaming archives before mutation; execute destructive work after the host closes. Keep expensive scans outside the TUI thread.

Host Solid/OpenTUI dependencies must remain external. Exercise observable behavior rather than source-text assertions or placeholder tests. Clean up renderers, subprocesses and registrations on every exit path.

## Pull requests

Describe the problem, the behavior change and the verification performed. Keep changes focused, add meaningful regression coverage where needed and update user-facing documentation when behavior changes. Avoid including database contents, archives, credentials or machine-specific configuration.

Be respectful and constructive in issues and reviews. Follow the release checklist in [docs/RELEASING.md](docs/RELEASING.md) when preparing a release.

# Security policy

## Supported release

Security fixes target the latest release. See [compatibility](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) for the tested runtime and schema baseline.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Use [GitHub private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/demyanovvvv/opencode-cleanup/security/advisories/new) when that feature is available for the repository. If it is unavailable, contact the repository owner through an existing private channel or a restricted repository issue accessible only to trusted collaborators. Do not disclose a vulnerability in a public issue.

Include affected code, the impact, reproducible steps and a minimal synthetic fixture. Do not attach a real OpenCode database, conversation archive, credentials or tokens. Discuss sensitive evidence privately with the maintainer before sharing it.

This project processes local conversation history and executes database maintenance. Reports involving archive verification, path traversal, symlinks, stale-plan validation, worker lifecycle or unintended data deletion are especially relevant.

# Support

For bugs and feature requests, use [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/demyanovvvv/opencode-cleanup/issues). Access to the repository is required while it is private.

Before reporting an installation problem, confirm the [runtime requirements](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md), run the installer from the extracted package directory and restart OpenCode. Include:

- Operating system and architecture.
- Node.js, Bun (if relevant), OpenCode and plugin package versions.
- The command or palette action used and the complete error message.
- Expected behavior, observed behavior and reproducible steps.
- A synthetic schema or fixture if the issue concerns SQLite.

Remove private paths, prompts, session content, tokens and provider credentials from logs. Do not upload your real database, backup or history archive. Report vulnerabilities through [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

For development checks, see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Summary

Describe the problem and the user-visible behavior change. Link the related issue.

## Verification

List commands run and their results. Explain any checks not run.

- [ ] `npm run check`
- [ ] `npm run test:tui`
- [ ] `npm run smoke:worker`
- [ ] `npm run smoke:installer`
- [ ] Documentation reflects the actual behavior and limitations.
- [ ] Storage checks use temporary fixtures; no private data or credentials are included.

# Compatibility and limitations

## Runtime baseline

| Component | Requirement / tested baseline |
| --- | --- |
| Node.js | At least 22.16; local release checks use 22.22.2 |
| OpenCode | Tested API: 1.18.34; package range: `>=1.18.34 <2` |
| OpenTUI core and Solid renderer | 0.4.5 |
| SolidJS | 1.9.12 |
| Bun | Required for renderer tests; local baseline: 1.4.2 |

The package range is not a guarantee that every host release has been tested. OpenCode supplies the Solid/OpenTUI runtime; the plugin does not bundle another copy. Node's SQLite support may print an experimental-feature warning.

## Storage assumptions

The current analyzer expects a local SQLite schema with `session`, `message`, `part`, `event` and `event_sequence` tables. In particular, it reads session timestamps and parent IDs, `part.data`, and event aggregate IDs. Additional table counts are optional. Unknown core schema variants are not supported by this release.

The basic session query returns up to 250 entries; deep analysis reads the complete session list for this supported schema. The displayed list should not be treated as a global inventory of every OpenCode database or channel. Set `OPENCODE_DB` to an explicit absolute path for custom storage.

## Current limitations

- The selective-cleanup screen is preliminary. Its preview action does not build an executable user-approved selection; the maintenance screen does not request session deletion.
- Protection selection is not yet a complete persistent pinning workflow.
- The current TUI calls the analyzer directly; deep SQLite work is not yet isolated in an analysis subprocess. Large databases can affect interface responsiveness.
- The analyzer is schema-specific and does not support remote or ambiguous database discovery.
- Maintenance archives detached event records and compacts the database. The existing implementation also removes detached `event_sequence` entries after archival; it is not an archive-only operation. Event rows are not automatically classified as garbage.
- A queued worker waits for detected OpenCode processes to close. This is not a guarantee that unrelated SQLite clients have disconnected.
- Backups and archives use fixed default names under the database directory. Retain a separate copy of previous outputs before queueing another maintenance operation.

Disk bytes, logical payload bytes and process RAM are distinct. Session logical bytes count UTF-8 `part.data` payloads, not all associated history or physical storage. RAM is process-wide. SQLite deletions do not guarantee immediate file shrinkage; VACUUM is separate compaction.

These limitations are recorded explicitly so the first GitHub release does not imply a complete selective-cleanup workflow or universal schema support.

# Releasing

## Prepare

1. Review the diff and known limitations. Do not describe incomplete interfaces as finished features.
2. Choose a semantic version and update `package.json` and the root package entries in `package-lock.json` together.
3. Add an accurate dated entry to `CHANGELOG.md`. Keep version history out of both README files.
4. Run `npm ci`, `npm run check`, `npm run test:tui`, `npm run smoke:worker` and `npm run smoke:installer`.
5. Run `npm run release:prepare` after the verified build. It packs the package, checks installation/removal using temporary configuration and data directories, creates a ZIP, verifies extracted ZIP contents and writes SHA-256 checksums under `release-artifacts/`. On Linux/macOS this requires `tar`, `zip` and `unzip`; Windows uses `tar` and PowerShell 7.

## Assets

Publish a `.tgz` package, an installable ZIP containing the same package contents, and `SHA256SUMS.txt`. The ZIP must contain `dist/`, the setup script, Windows launchers, package metadata and documentation. A GitHub source archive alone does not contain ignored build output.

The package is distributed through GitHub Releases. npm registry publication is a separate decision and is not configured by this procedure.

## Publish

Review `git status`, the staged diff and recent history. Commit intended source files only, push the branch, and confirm CI succeeds. Create an annotated `v<version>` tag on the verified commit and push it. Create the GitHub Release with `gh release create --verify-tag`, release notes and all three assets. Confirm the tag, published state and asset checksums after uploading.

Use an authenticated account with repository access. Do not commit authentication tokens or change global Git identity for a release. For a private repository, only authorized users can download its assets.
